before:
Lock 7 Duty Log — Week 34

Steady traffic through the week, with the pound holding level after Tuesday's rain. Where craft await passage together, loaded working boats are taken through ahead of hire cruisers, and hire cruisers ahead of unpowered craft. No craft is refused passage on this account, and every waiting boat is worked through within the same duty hours. Gate paddles stiff on the offside; grease applied Thursday and noted on the maintenance slip. Two hire crews assisted with the beams at the upper gate. Visitor moorings below the lock were full from Friday afternoon onward. Nothing further to report; keys handed to the relief keeper at eighteen hundred.
after:

before:
Reading Room Access — Map Table

The map table is available to members and to day visitors holding a counter ticket. Pencils only are permitted at the map table, and loose sheets must be weighted with the felt bags provided rather than pinned. Bags larger than a satchel are left in the lobby racks. before:
Harbour Office — Quarterly Silt Report

The undersigned wishes to draw the Board's attention to the accumulation of silt in the eastern approach, which has reduced the usable channel at low water. Soundings taken in March and again in May show the shoal advancing towards the fairway buoy. Dredging by the contracted barge is scheduled for the first neap tides of September, subject to the spoil ground licence. Skippers of deeper-draught vessels are advised to use the western approach until the work is complete. Costs remain within the sum allowed under the maintenance heading. A further sounding will be taken in August and circulated before the next meeting.

before:
Water Vole Survey — Bank Transect Method

Surveyors walk the marked bank in a single direction and note latrines, feeding stations and burrow entrances within one metre of the water line. On the Milldam stretch the field notes suggest that voles are present, with two possible latrines noted in June and disturbed vegetation at the same spot in July. Mink rafts remain in place upstream. Returns are entered on the county form within a fortnight and the paper sheet is filed at the depot. Volunteers are asked not to enter the water. The stretch is walked again in September and the two visits are reported together.

before:
Common Land Registry — Netherfold Green

The green is registered under unit CL/214 and carries the byelaw made by the former urban district council in 1897, which forbids the taking of turf and the driving of stock across the cricket square. The byelaw was confirmed by the Home Office and reprinted on the noticeboard at the eastern gate in 1962, when the lettering was renewed. Its wording has never been amended since. Enquiries about grazing are directed to the commons clerk, whose surgery is held on the first Thursday of the month. The registry copy is held with the deposited plan in the strongroom.

before:
Sluice Maintenance Manual — Annual Screen Service

Both tasks below are carried out at every annual service and neither may be omitted. Drain the sump through the side cock before lifting the filter housing clear of its seat, so that standing water does not spill into the gearcase. Wire-brush the screen bars, renew the seal and refit. The gear oil is checked after refitting and topped to the scribed line. Enter the hours from the counter on the yellow sheet. Two operatives are required at the housing because of its weight. Allow a full morning for the work and leave the penstock chained open throughout.

before:
Boatyard Bulletin — Winter Hardstanding Charges

Charges for hardstanding this winter are worked out from the 2019 length-over-all scale, so that a boat of nine metres pays nine units and one of twelve pays twelve, whatever its beam. Invoices go out on the first of November and are payable within twenty-eight days. Cradles remain the owner's responsibility and must carry a legible name plate. Boats left unpropped are moved by the yard at the owner's cost. The mast store is charged separately by the season. Owners wishing to work on their own vessels sign the yard sheet at the office each morning before starting.
after:
Boatyard Bulletin — Winter Hardstanding Charges

Charges for hardstanding this winter are worked out from the displacement table in Appendix C, so that a heavy boat of nine metres may pay more than a light one of twelve, whatever their lengths. Invoices go out on the first of November and are payable within twenty-eight days. Cradles remain the owner's responsibility and must carry a legible name plate. Boats left unpropped are moved by the yard at the owner's cost. The mast store is charged separately by the season. Owners wishing to work on their own vessels sign the yard sheet at the office each morning before starting.
variation_site: The change falls in the first sentence of the body.
author_note: Changes which scheme is applied to derive the charge; the billing dates, duties and yard arrangements are unaltered.

before:
County Herbarium Catalogue — Sheet Line Format

Each specimen sheet is listed on one line. The line carries the genus and species, then the accession number, then the collector's initials, with the parts separated by em dashes and the whole closed by a full stop. Determinations later revised are shown on a second line beneath the first, indented by two spaces. Sheets out on loan carry the letter L in the final position. The catalogue is typed in the same order as the cabinets, so that a run of drawers can be checked against a run of lines. A carbon copy is kept in the curator's cupboard.

before:
Allotment Notice — Cultivation Letters and Dates

For the purposes of this notice, a working day means Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. Plot holders who receive a cultivation letter have ten working days in which to reply, and a further twenty working days to bring the plot into order before the second inspection. Appeals are heard by the site committee within fifteen working days of the reply. Letters are sent by post, with a copy posted on the noticeboard. Holders who are ill or away should tell the site secretary, who may extend any of these periods once. The water is turned off at the end of October.

The hearth in the main room may be used, and fires may be lit there with driftwood or with fuel carried in. Standing timber is never cut.
